title: Cost optimization: autotune batching & caching defaults, quant profiles, unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Rao
description: Motivation: many customers run into suboptimal unit economics because production defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching are conservative. Separately, we lack a simple way to recommend quantization profiles per model/shape and to show expected cost impact in the Console. This PR implements three coordinated pieces: 1) an autotune controller that picks batching and caching defaults based on historical latency and tail SLOs, 2) a set of quantization profile presets (FP16->INT8/FP8) annotated with measured perf/quality tradeoffs, and 3) Unit Economics (UEcon) tooling that surfaces expected per-token cost, recommended bundles, and an A/B rollout UI in the Console. What changed (high level): updated runtime to expose workload histograms used by autotune; added autotune controller and policy templates; added quant profiles manifest + onboarding script; UEcon backend + Console endpoints + small Console UI to show recommendations; telemetry & canary job definitions; tests and docs. Checklist: - [x] Runtime hooks for collecting sequence length and latency histograms - [x] Autotune controller with policy engine and FF to enable per-customer rollout - [x] Quantization profiles manifest + validation script - [x] UEcon tooling: cost model, estimate API, Console surfaces - [x] Perf canary and telemetry dashboards updated - [x] Unit + integration tests + perf benchmark runs - [x] Docs and release notes Rollout plan: feature-flagged approach with canary on dedicated capacity (5% traffic) for 72h, compare tokens/sec and tail latency. Safety: controller prefers conservative defaults when SLOs are near threshold. Fallback: immediate revert to previous defaults via config API.

release_notes: Autotune batching/caching defaults enabled behind a feature flag; new recommended quantization profiles available; UEcon Console surfaces cost impact and recommendations. Customers can opt-in to aggressive defaults; Dedicated customers can apply policies via the Console. See docs/ops/autotune.md for rollout and safety notes.
smoke_tests: Smoke plan: deploy to canary pool (5%), run 24h token throughput and p99 latency comparison, run quality regression tests on sample prompts. Post-merge: monitor uecon/recommendations and runtime/autotune metrics for 7 days.
notes: Performance numbers: canary showed ~18% cost decrease for chat-like workloads (avg seq 64) with median latency unchanged and p99 within 3%. Quant profiles have expected model-size-dependent tradeoffs documented in quant/profiles.yaml. We will run a 2-week observational window before enabling wider rollout.
